features.name: Zig 0.17-dev resolved and locked by Pantry
features.notes: The exact compiler build is locked locally and in CI.

features.name: No Git submodules
features.notes: Sibling repositories are locked by commit and checked out directly in CI.

features.name: Allocator, ownership, concurrency, feature, and atomic hot-reload contracts
features.notes: Runtime publication pins in-flight requests to immutable generations; reclamation, errors, feature discovery, and connector responsibilities are explicit and tested.

features.name: Five inspection phases plus logging lifecycle
features.notes: Connection setup is pre-phase; the five stable phase numbers, legal transitions, early exits, terminal drop behavior, and exactly-once logging finalization are enforced.

features.name: Detection-only interventions
features.notes: Interventions preserve evidence, are marked non-enforcing, and do not interrupt or terminate detection-only transactions. Detailed action precedence remains scoped to WAF-15.

features.name: Bounded scalar transaction variables with phase availability and origins
features.notes: The 78-name stable scalar registry, aliases, origins, phase gates, connection/request/response producers, UTC timing, monotonic duration, body diagnostics, identity, persistent RESOURCE binding, matched values, and minimum-severity semantics are executable. Full buffered body materialization remains WAF-24/WAF-28.

features.name: Bounded collections, targets, exclusions, counts, origins, and runtime macros
features.notes: The 37-namespace registry, bounded owned storage, repeated/map mutations, source offsets, phase gates, exact and zig-regex selectors, exclusions, counts, explicit matcher errors, and configured baseline macro semantics are executable. HTTP/body/XML producers and persistent backends remain in their linked downstream issues.

features.name: libinjection SQLi and XSS detection
features.notes: @detectSQLi and @detectXSS use the full libinjection port in zig-injection (a byte-exact translation of libinjection-go v0.3.2 validated against the pinned 54-case SQLi and 118-case folding corpora and the libinjection XSS differential vectors). They pass the retained Coraza detectSQLi and detectXSS corpora. Allocation-free with reusable per-worker scratch.

features.name: Numeric, string, and regex scalar operators
features.notes: eq/ge/gt/le/lt, beginsWith/endsWith/contains/strmatch/within/streq/containsWord, and rx/rxGlobal/rsub resolve case-insensitively to a typed union. Numeric parsing preserves the ModSecurity std::stoi and Coraza strconv.Atoi profiles; rx exposes capture fields 0..9, bounded compile and runtime errors, empty-pattern always-match, and optional per-worker LRU memoization. rsub preserves the pinned ModSecurity 3.0.16 always-true stub. Evidence covers the 118-case Coraza operator corpus and ReleaseFast benchmarks. Engine rule-evaluation wiring and detectSQLi/detectXSS parity remain separate issues.

features.name: Encoding and byte-range validation operators
features.notes: validateByteRange (compiled allowed-byte set with empty-arg always-match), validateUtf8Encoding, and validateUrlEncoding match the pinned Coraza semantics and pass the retained 53-case corpus. GeoIP, RBL, GSB, fuzzy-hash, file-inspection, national-identifier, and schema validation operators remain later slices of WAF-20, several gated on external data or the XML subsystem.

features.name: Phrase (Aho-Corasick) and IP CIDR operators
features.notes: pm/pmFromFile/pmFromDataset compile to an ASCII case-insensitive Aho-Corasick automaton with O(1)-per-byte membership, bounded state counts, empty-pattern always-match, and a non-overlapping capture iterator. ipMatch/ipMatchFromFile/ipMatchFromDataset parse IPv4 and zero-compressed IPv6 CIDR subnets with the pinned bare-address /32 and /128 defaults, unparseable-token skipping, and Go net.To4 IPv4-mapped normalization. Evidence replays the retained Coraza pm (15) and ipMatch (3623) corpora with fuzz and ReleaseFast benchmarks. Dataset registry and reload wiring land with the engine dataset subsystem.

features.name: Query-string argument and cookie parsing
features.notes: processUri parses the query string into ARGS_GET/ARGS with the pinned Coraza doParseQuery split and x-www-form-urlencoded queryUnescape, honoring SecArgumentSeparator; addRequestHeader parses the Cookie header into REQUEST_COOKIES (Netscape format, the only format either baseline parses — SecCookieFormat 1 is rejected rather than accepted and silently parsed as format 0). Body arguments populate ARGS_POST through the URLENCODED/JSON/MULTIPART/XML processors. A malformed percent-escape in a query or body argument name or value raises URLENCODED_ERROR while still decoding non-strictly, matching both baselines. Duplicate and conflicting framing headers stay visible in REQUEST_HEADERS so a rule can detect request smuggling; rejecting the request is the proxy's decision, not the WAF's. PATH_INFO, REQUEST_FILENAME, REQUEST_BASENAME, and SERVER_NAME (port and IPv6-bracket aware) are published from the request target and Host header.

features.name: Bounded request-body buffering and processors
features.notes: The request body is buffered in memory up to the request-body limit and exposed as REQUEST_BODY (honoring SecRequestBodyAccess), with a reject/process-partial policy and a spool-sink boundary for disk spooling. The URLENCODED, JSON, MULTIPART, and XML body processors run against the buffered body. URLENCODED/JSON populate ARGS_POST (JSON flattened into dotted json.* keys with array-length entries, matching Coraza); multipart file parts fill FILES/FILES_NAMES/FILES_SIZES/FILES_COMBINED_SIZE and MULTIPART_NAME/MULTIPART_FILENAME/MULTIPART_PART_HEADERS pinned to ModSecurity's multipart processor; XML populates the XML collection under //@* (attribute values) and /* (text/CDATA) via the zig-xml tokenizer, matching Coraza and OWASP CRS. Spooling is a connector responsibility through the Sink boundary — the request path never blocks on a filesystem, and where uploads may be written and whether they outlive the transaction are deployment decisions — with request_buffer.FileSink supplied so a connector need not reimplement it, and addFileMetadata publishing FILES_TMPNAMES from the names the connector actually used.

features.name: Response-header and body inspection
features.notes: Response headers populate RESPONSE_HEADERS/RESPONSE_CONTENT_TYPE and the response body is buffered and exposed as RESPONSE_BODY (honoring SecResponseBodyAccess). The response JSON body processor is opt-in via ctl:responseBodyProcessor (Coraza does no Content-Type auto-detection for responses) and flattens the body into RESPONSE_ARGS with the same dotted json.* keys and array-length entries as the request side, publishing RES_BODY_PROCESSOR and raising RES_BODY_PROCESSOR_ERROR on invalid JSON. Response-body mutation and content injection remain.

features.name: Native, legacy JSON, JSON, and OCSF audit-log formats
features.notes: A transaction snapshots into an AuditRecord (identity, connection endpoints, request line, request/response headers from their collections, bodies, status, timestamp, interruption, and part-H rule messages formatted in ModSecurity's RuleMessage::log layout) and serializes via serializeAuditLog in four formats honoring SecAuditLogParts: native serial (pinned to ModSecurity toOldAuditLogFormat), structured JSON and legacy JSON (Coraza schemas), and OCSF v1.2.0 Web Resources Activity (Coraza OCSF formatter). Delivery uses an I/O-free Sink boundary with serial, callback, and ModSecurity concurrent-layout writers (src/audit_writer.zig). Redaction is a zig-waf extension over both baselines rather than a port: ModSecurity 3.0.16's parser rejects every sanitise action outright ("is not yet supported", seclang-parser.yy) and Coraza 3.7.0 has none. Implemented here are: sanitizeRequestHeader/sanitizeResponseHeader mask header values with same-length '*', sanitizeArg masks an argument value in the request body, and sanitizeMatched masks the matched variable. sanitizeMatchedBytes is rejected at compile time rather than accepted and ignored, matching the baselines and refusing to let a rule look as though it redacts a secret while writing it out in full. Debug-log/Prometheus/OpenTelemetry telemetry is WAF-31.

features.name: Revisioned TX and persistent IP, SESSION, USER, GLOBAL, and RESOURCE collections
features.notes: Bounded transaction-local mutation, persistent initialization, expiry-only state, optimistic conflict rebasing, typed fail-open/fail-closed behavior, thread-safe in-memory storage, and Pantry-linked LMDB storage are executable. SecLang text parsing and action-plan wiring consume these APIs in WAF-10 through WAF-15.

features.name: Versioned C connector ABI
features.notes: Opaque ownership, sized structs, rule-set loading (zig_waf_create_with_rules compiles a SecLang config), the full transaction lifecycle, autonomous phase evaluation (zig_waf_transaction_evaluate_phase), feature discovery, errors, intervention retrieval, and audit-log serialization (zig_waf_transaction_serialize_audit_log + zig_waf_free) are implemented — the complete seam a native data plane (e.g. the rpx dataplane) links against to run traffic through the engine. The C smoke test drives the full flow (rules -> request -> evaluate -> 403). Callbacks and the ABI compatibility matrix remain.

features.name: Config validate, explain, and version CLI
features.notes: The zig-waf CLI parses, compiles, and directive-validates SecLang configs (validate), lists compiled rules with phase/id/action/location (explain), runs a synthetic request through the engine and reports the block/allow decision (test), and reports the version, exiting non-zero on rejection so rule sets can be gated in CI. The format, replay, and benchmark subcommands remain.

features.name: Immutable cache-efficient structural execution plans
features.notes: Owned typed IR, phase indexes, defaults, chains, action families, conservative prefilters, immutable macro programs, stable diagnostics, deterministic fingerprints, atomic component sharing, WAF generation pinning, corpus compilation, fuzzing, and ReleaseFast metrics are verified. WAF-12 owns complete directive-specific semantic validation.

features.name: Autonomous rule-execution engine
features.notes: The engine evaluates a rule set against a request on its own, in layers: rule_eval dispatches compile-free operators by name; RuntimeOperator compiles @rx/@pm/@ipMatch once and reuses them; Transaction.resolveTarget maps a variable name plus key selector to values (with the &count form); Transaction.evaluateRule resolves a rule's targets, applies its transformation pipeline, and runs the operator with !@op negation; and Transaction.evaluatePhase walks every executable head in a phase, evaluates whole chains, applies a fully-matched chain atomically, and halts on an enforced disruptive decision. Exposed to connectors as zig_waf_transaction_evaluate_phase. Verified end to end: a SQLi request is denied while a benign request passes. multiMatch checkpoints, macro-expanded operator arguments, and regex key selectors remain.

features.name: Rule defaults, removals, updates, markers, and authenticated remote rules
features.notes: Phase-scoped defaults, ID/tag/message removal, ordered target and action overlays, source-ordered marker linking, explicit missing-rule policy, and authenticated bounded remote assembly are immutable compile-time behavior. Pinned upstream-derived fixtures, allocation-failure tests, deterministic fuzzing, corpus gates, and baseline/overlay ReleaseFast measurements are executable.

features.name: Typed metadata, non-disruptive effects, captures, persistence, and owned event intent
features.notes: Metadata and effect text compile once; standalone rules and complete chains apply through bounded atomic local/persistent staging. Post-action owned intent, capture replacement, transaction-local ENV, checked TX/persistent arithmetic, binding, expiry, deterministic decay, failure policy, differential fixtures, fuzzing, and latency/allocation benchmarks are executable.

features.name: Typed disruptive decisions, flow cursor, and transaction runtime controls
features.notes: Atomic decisions, allow scopes, skip/skipAfter, transaction-local engine/audit/body controls, exact rule-tag and exact/bounded zig-regex rule-target exclusions, capability-gated proxy, exhaustive allocation rollback, fuzzing, and ReleaseFast decision/cursor/exclusion benchmarks are executable. Pause duration parsing and execution remain explicitly assigned to WAF-21.

features.name: Stable transformation union, aliases, ordered pipelines, and bounded caching
features.notes: All 35 typed kinds, two American-spelling aliases, and the compile-time none reset resolve case-insensitively, execute in published plan order with multiMatch checkpoints and bounded transaction caching, and preserve profile-specific ModSecurity and Coraza byte semantics. Evidence covers the 355-case retained Coraza corpus, per-kind differential vectors, upstream inventory drift, deterministic fuzzing, and ReleaseFast hot-path benchmarks with zero steady-state allocation. Plugin transformation execution remains assigned to WAF-22.

features.name: Pantry-managed PostgreSQL 18 and native libpq 18
features.notes: Packages are locked and the client links native libpq 18. Per-project cluster/port isolation and the documented production deployment profile are still required (#51).

features.name: STX development and embedded production assets
features.notes: The workspace and pinned STX source exist; the fingerprinted asset compiler remains.

features.name: HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy
features.notes: Standalone data-plane implementation has not started.

features.name: HTTP/2 reverse proxy through nghttp2
features.notes: The adapter is scheduled after HTTP/1.1 framing and backpressure.

features.name: Constrained fleet schema with range partitions and transactional migrations
features.notes: Append-only migrations, each in its own transaction; roles, credentials, and saved searches constrained by the schema rather than by callers; security_events range-partitioned on occurred_at with BRIN on the timestamp and GIN on jsonb.

features.name: libpq client with prepared statements, timeouts, cancellation, retries, and per-workload pools
features.notes: Values are bound as text parameters throughout; binary format is deliberately unused because it would move timestamptz encoding onto the client. API, rollout, and ingestion have separate bounded pools so one cannot starve another.

features.name: Ed25519-signed policy bundles, staged rollout, health gates, and drift detection
features.notes: Signing is asymmetric so nodes hold only the public key; verification fails closed. A rollout widens only when the cohort already on the version is responsive and has confirmed it; a node that has never reported counts as drifted.

features.name: Idempotent, zstd-compressed durable event queue with COPY ingestion and reconnect
features.notes: Re-sent batches deduplicate by (event_key, occurred_at); drain switches to COPY at the measured 24-event crossover (zig build bench-ingestion); snapshots survive an upgrade across format versions.

features.name: Partition-pruned search, cursor pagination, retention, CSV export, and capacity forecasts
features.notes: Pagination is by (occurred_at, id) cursor, so a growing stream neither repeats nor skips rows. A stream with no measurable growth reports no forecast rather than a fabricated one.

features.name: SQLite mirror of the fleet repositories for demos and server-free tests
features.notes: Mirrors the repository contracts and their guarantees (immutable versions, drift). Carries no fleet guarantees and is not a deployment target; signed bundles are deliberately not mirrored.

features.name: Local authentication, RBAC, API tokens, sessions, and OIDC ID-token verification
features.notes: argon2id for passwords, SHA-256 for 256-bit generated credentials. Authorization is a total function over enumerated actions. OIDC takes the algorithm from the key, not the token header, so alg:none and HMAC confusion fail.

features.name: Alert thresholds, deduplication, silences, signed webhooks, retry accounting, and Prometheus metrics
features.notes: Firing is one statement, so concurrent dispatchers deliver one alert. A metric that cannot be collected is omitted rather than reported as zero.

features.name: Streaming JSON body processor with bounded depth and duplicate-key exposure
features.notes: Flattens by streaming rather than materializing a value tree. A duplicated key publishes every value under the same argument, because parsers disagree about which one wins and inspecting only one leaves the other unfiltered; refusing such a body would publish no arguments at all, making one repeated key a bypass. Nesting is bounded by SecRequestBodyJsonDepthLimit (Coraza's 1024 default), since flattening costs a frame per level. A truncated body is inspected as far as it was read and reports REQBODY_PROCESSOR_ERROR. Dotted json.* keys, array indices, and array-length entries match Coraza.

features.name: Host extension registry for operators and body processors
features.notes: Operators and body processors a host registers, called where the configuration names them. An extension nothing provides fails to compile rather than leaving a rule that never matches or a body nothing reads. An operator plugin reports unavailable distinctly from no-match and the engine counts it, so a data source that failed to load is visible instead of reading as clean traffic. Transformations, actions, and directives are deliberately closed — their semantics are the compatibility surface — and the C ABI (#33) is the cross-language boundary rather than an embedded WASM runtime.
